nodes.title: fix: make TimePass.parse optional in types and docs

data.title: Bug: stats `TimePass.parse` is missing when a processor returns no code blocks
data.titleHTML: Bug: stats TimePass.parse is missing when a processor returns no code blocks
data.bodyHTML:
Environment

Node version: v24.19.0
npm version: v11.17.0
Local ESLint version: v10.9.1
Global ESLint version: Not found
Operating System: darwin 24.6.0

What parser are you using?

Default (Espree)

What did you do?

Repro code

import { ESLint } from "eslint";

const eslint = new ESLint({
    overrideConfigFile: true,
    stats: true,
    overrideConfig: [
        {
            files: ["**/*.txt"],
            processor: {
                preprocess() {
                    return [];
                },
                postprocess() {
                    return [];
                }
            }
        }
    ]
});

const [result] = await eslint.lintText("plain text", {
    filePath: "empty.txt"
});

console.log(JSON.stringify(result.stats, null, 2));

What did you expect to happen?

Every entry in stats.times.passes should satisfy ESLint's documented
TimePass shape.

{
  "parse": {
    "total": 0
  },
  "fix": {
    "total": 0
  },
  "total": 0.293166
}

And in types file:

eslint/lib/types/index.d.ts

Lines 1125 to 1146 in 87e0a08

interface TimePass {
/**
* The parse object containing all parse time information.
*/
parse: { total: number };
/**
* The rules object containing all lint time information for each rule.
*/
rules?: Record<string, { total: number }>;
/**
* The fix object containing all fix time information.
*/
fix: { total: number };
/**
* The total time that is spent on (parsing, fixing, linting) a file.
*/
total: number;
}
}

What actually happened?

{
  "times": {
    "passes": [
      {
        "fix": {
          "total": 0
        },
        "total": 0.286208
      }
    ]
  },
  "fixPasses": 0
}

Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

https://github.com/ntnyq/repro-eslint-time-stats

Participation

  • I am willing to submit a pull request for this issue.

AI acknowledgment

  • I did not use AI to generate this issue report.
  • (If the above is not checked) I have reviewed the AI-generated content before submitting.

Additional comments

No response

node.bodyHTML:
Thanks for the report, I can reproduce this.

Since in this case there is no parsing, I think it really makes more sense to omit the property, as it currently works. We'd just update the docs and types to align with the current behavior.

@eslint/eslint-team thoughts?

node.body:
Agree with just updating docs & types. Marking this as accepted for the docs.

@ntnyq Feel free to send a PR updating docs & types to match current behaviour
